title: friction-metrics-pulse-and-candidate-bits-2026-06-11
body:
Purpose: quick pulse on operational friction we’re seeing in production customers + a compact set of candidate features/probes to test in the next two sprints. This is a working note — rough, prioritized by estimated customer impact x likelihood.

High-level takeaway (TL;DR)
- Two clusters dominate ~72% of actionable friction: (A) generation latency / sporadic tail latency leading to user retries; (B) unpredictable quality regressions after model rollouts (small but high-noise).
- Quick wins available: routing fallback policy tweak, one-off prefix-cache warmers, and a lightweight rollout guard based on per-prompt eval thresholds.

Data snapshot (last 30 days, aggregated across top-20 paying tenants)
- Median response latency: 320ms (up 12% vs. prior window)
- 95th pct latency: 1.6s (spiky; correlates with bursts at 11:00–13:00 PT for two customers)
- Retry events (client-side): +18% month-over-month; common cause: perceived slow responses or truncated streams
- Post-rollout complaint rate: ~0.9% of sessions (content quality flags), but concentrated in 4 large customers (BankBlue, EduSoft corp, MarketplaceX, Researchly)
- Incidents flagged to CS: 14 (7 latency, 5 quality, 2 auth/permission edgecases)

Customer-quoted behavior samples (anonymized)
- "It just stalls sometimes and the UI gives up; users hit submit again and sometimes get duplicates." — MarketplaceX PM
- "After you pushed the new model, our summaries got shorter and missed the ‘what matters’ bits. Our reviewers got noisy." — Researchly ops lead
- "Embedding similarity drift: related-doc suggestions are now off by a lot for our taxonomy." — EduSoft product owner

Observed clusters (heuristic grouping)
1) Tail-latency bursts: correlated with heavy long-sequence requests + small batch windows. Appears during predictable business hours for two customers.
2) Quiet quality regressions after model variant rollouts: small but focused on specific prompt templates (summaries, multi-doc synthesis).
3) Routing incompatibilities: requests routed to quantized model variant without matching tokenization/config leading to formatting artifacts.
4) UX/backoff mismatches: frontend clients assume shorter SLOs and retry aggressively, amplifying load and tail latency.

Candidate features / probes (ranked by impact x effort)
- Fast fallback routing (LOW effort, HIGH impact)
  quick description: add a rule to detect sustained latency > SLO for a route and automatically fallback to a compatible lower-latency variant (same quality family) for 5m.
  immediate test: enable for MarketplaceX beta route, monitor retry rate and 95th-latency.
  owner: Marcus Li

- Prefix cache warmer (MED effort, MED impact)
  quick description: allow customers to configure a small set of prompts (or sampled recent prompts) to prepopulate KV cache on scale-ups/instance attach.
  why: reduces cold-KV bursts that correlate with 95th spikes.
  risk: storage/eviction policy tradeoffs.
  owner: Priya Sharma

- Per-prompt quality gate for rollouts (MED effort, HIGH impact)
  quick description: require new model variants to pass a tiny per-customer prompt set (10–50 prompts) with automated quality checks before global traffic ramp. Failure triggers automatic canary rollback.
  quick probe: integrate with existing rollout engine for two internal customers first.
  owner: Ibrahim Hassan

- Client backoff guidelines + SDK patch (LOW effort, MED impact)
  quick description: publish explicit retry/backoff guidance; ship minor SDK change to default to jittered exponential backoff and idempotency tokens for common endpoints.
  owner: Leah Park (with DevEx)

- Diagnostic mini-traces for long sequences (MED effort, LOW immediate impact)
  quick description: lightweight per-request trace that samples KV cache hits, batch size, queueing time; surfaced in Console as an 'explain latency' button for affected requests.
  owner: Observability team (TBD)

Quick experiment plan (2-week cadence)
Week 1: Enable Fast fallback routing for MarketplaceX (canary to 5% of their traffic) + SDK backoff doc + internal retro after 5 business days.
Week 2: Run prefix-cache warmer as a scoped experiment on an internal replica of EduSoft’s workload; collect 95th-latency delta.
Parallel: Start per-prompt quality gate PoC with Researchly’s 30 prompt set. Aim to have gating results in the rollout dashboard.

Success metrics (what we’ll watch)
- Retry events down 25% on pilot routes
- 95th latency down >= 20% on affected tenants for prefix-warm runs
- Post-rollout quality complaint rate reduced by >= 50% for canary-gated rollouts

Open questions & risks (notes-to-self)
- How to manage prefix cache state across autoscaling churn without causing memory blowouts? (engineering constraints)
- Will fallback routing cause quality regression for customers with tightly tuned prompts? Need per-route configurable thresholds.
- Can we operationalize per-customer prompt sets without heavy manual work? Consider a lightweight prompt-capture UI in Console.

Immediate asks for this doc (who does what next)
- Marcus: schedule a 30m design call with infra + serving-runtime to sketch fallback rule implementation (by 2026-06-17).
- Priya: prototype a minimal prefix-warm CLI that accepts a small file of prompts; run against internal trace dataset (by 2026-06-22).
- Ibrahim: scope the rollout-gate requirements and list existing rollout engine touchpoints (by 2026-06-18).
- Leah: draft SDK backoff patch and update integration guide (by 2026-06-19).

Notes, edge thoughts (informal)
- Some customers would accept slightly lower per-token quality if it reduced latency and cost — consider offering an explicit 'low-latency' tuning knob.
- For embedding drift, quick diagnostic: compute centroid shift over rolling 7-day window for each collection. If > threshold, trigger retrain/refresh suggestions to customer.
- Keep an eye on billing anomalies when we route to different quantized families — customers have raised cost surprises.

References / evidence snippets
- Pager log excerpt (June 4): repeated queueing events on node pool g2-high for MarketplaceX; correlates with long sequence batch starts. (See JIRA CS-4821 for dump)
- Customer emails: Researchly summary drop complaints captured in ticket CORE-3029.
- Internal Slack: #cs-field-probes thread with user repro steps (June 7)

Appendix: quick sketch of rollout-gate flow (brainstorm)
- capture: per-customer prompt set (up to 50 prompts) + automatic selection heuristics (recent top queries)
- evaluate: run new variant over set; compute pass rates for thresholded metrics (BLEU-ish / rouge / embedding drift / ranked callback)
- decision: if pass rate >= x% then continue ramp; else hold and notify account owner

——
This doc is intentionally concise and operational-focused. Use comments below to record observations from QA sessions and customer follow-ups.

Comments / in-line reactions (please add)
- Marcus: "Agree fallback rule looks promising; need to ensure we preserve traceability for audits."
- Priya: "Will prototype prefix warmer using small LRU with TTL and per-tenant caps."
- Ibrahim: "We should coordinate gating with product rollouts — could be a blocker otherwise."

Next update: target 2026-06-22 after initial experiments finish.

-- Leah
